title: Altered Mental Status
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is an elderly patient presenting with the classic triad of normal pressure hydrocephalus: (1) gait disturbance ('magnetic gait' — feet feel stuck to floor), (2) urinary incontinence, and (3) progressive cognitive decline/dementia. NPH is one of the few reversible causes of dementia and must be recognized early. CT/MRI shows ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal atrophy, without obstruction. LP opening pressure is NORMAL (<18 cm H2O) — this distinguishes NPH from obstructive hydrocephalus. High-volume LP (30-50 mL CSF removal) with pre- and post- gait assessment is diagnostic: improvement in gait after CSF removal supports the diagnosis and predicts response to VP shunting. Definitive treatment: ventriculoperitoneal shunt.
chief_complaint: Gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, cognitive decline

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: Gait assessment — magnetic gait, wide-based, shuffling. Cognitive: MMSE for baseline.

stacks.label: CT head without contrast / MRI brain
stacks.finding: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal atrophy. No obstruction. Evans' index >0.3.

stacks.label: Lumbar puncture (high-volume, 30-50 mL)
stacks.finding: Normal opening pressure (<18 cm H2O). CSF analysis to rule out other causes. Post-LP gait assessment — improvement supports NPH diagnosis.

stacks.label: TSH, B12, RPR
stacks.finding: Rule out reversible causes of dementia (hypothyroidism, B12 deficiency, neurosyphilis).

stacks.label: Neurosurgery consult / VP shunt
stacks.finding: Definitive treatment: ventriculoperitoneal shunt. Best results if early intervention before irreversible damage.

physical_exam.neurological: Triad: magnetic gait (shuffling, feet stuck to floor) + urinary incontinence + cognitive decline. MMSE decreased. No focal deficits. Reflexes normal.

decoys.label: Alzheimer's diagnosis without NPH workup
decoys.reason_wrong: NPH is one of the FEW reversible causes of dementia. Classic triad + ventriculomegaly on imaging must prompt LP and consideration of VP shunting. Missing this condemns patient to irreversible decline.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Wet, wacky, wobbly' = urinary incontinence + cognitive decline + gait disturbance. Ventriculomegaly WITHOUT obstruction. Normal LP opening pressure.
Remove 30-50 mL CSF. Gait improvement after LP predicts good response to VP shunting. This is a reversible cause of dementia.
Ventriculoperitoneal shunt diverts CSF. Early intervention prevents irreversible neurological damage.

case_summary: NPH: classic triad + ventriculomegaly with normal LP opening pressure. High-volume LP shows gait improvement → VP shunt placed by neurosurgery. Reversible dementia — must recognize early.
